'''Juan Manuel Lozano Mejía''' ([[Mexico City]], 12 December 1929 – Mexico City, 10 October 2007) was a recognized Mexican physicist. He was one of the pioneers of nuclear physics in Mexico and an academic at [[National Autonomous University of Mexico|Universidad Nacional Autónoma de México]] for over fifty years.

== Biography ==
He carried out his bachelor's and doctoral studies in Physics at the [[School of Sciences, UNAM]] from 1947 to 1952, at its original campus ([[Palacio de Minería]]). His theses were the following: ''Dynamical description of a potential dispersion'' (1953)<ref>{{Cite web |title=Descripción dinámica de la dispersión por un potencial |url=http://132.248.9.195/pmig2020/0066509/Index.html |access-date=2023-09-21 |language=es}}</ref> and ''Causal description and dispersion relations'' (1960) <ref>{{Cite web |title=Descripción causal y relaciones de dispersión |url=http://132.248.9.195/ptd2015/anteriores/ciencias/0724743/Index.html|access-date=2023-09-21 |language=es}}</ref> [translated from spanish: ''Descripción dinámica de la dispersión por un potencial'' and ''Descripción causal y relaciones de dispersión''], both were directed by Professor [[Marcos Moshinsky]].

His academic and professional career began as a professor at the School of Sciences and as a researcher at the Physics Institute at UNAM after the university's main campus changed to [[Ciudad Universitaria, Mexico City|Ciudad Universitaria]]. He was the director of the School of Sciences, UNAM, from 1969 to 1973. He also worked for some time at the ''Observatorio Astronómico Nacional'' (Spanish for National Astronomy Observatory) at UNAM and the ''Instituto Nacional de Investigación Científica'' (Spanish for National Institute of Scientific Research), the latter of which would then become the [[Consejo Nacional de Ciencia y Tecnología (Mexico)|Consejo Nacional de Humanidades, Ciencias y Tecnologías]] (Spanish for National Council of Humanities Science and Technology).<ref name=":0">{{Cite web |title=AHUNAM |url=http://www.ahunam.unam.mx/consultar_fcu?id=3.34 |access-date=2023-09-29 |website=www.ahunam.unam.mx}}</ref>

His knowledge of the educational, scientific, and cultural environment would lead him to participate in the creation and operation of several national institutions, such as the ''Colegio de Ciencias y Humanidades'' (Spanish for ''School of Science and Humanities''), ''Colegio de Bachilleres'' (Mexican public high school system), and the ''[[Universidad Autónoma Metropolitana]]'' (Spanish for ''Metropolitan Autonomous University'').<ref name=":1">{{Cite web |last1=Torres Monroy |first1=Luis |last2=González Hernández |first2=Luis Carlos |date=2013 |title=Guía específica del fondo Juan Manuel Lozano Mejía |url=http://www.ahunam.unam.mx/instrumentos_d/3.34.pdf |access-date=October 9, 2023 |website=ahunam}}</ref>

He was also a founder of the [[Mexican Physical Society]] (1950)<ref>{{Cite book |last=Domínguez |first=Raúl |title=Historia de la física nuclear en México: 1933-1963 |date=2000 |publisher=Plaza y Valdes |isbn=978-968-856-873-6 |location=México |pages=105}}</ref> and the precursor organization for the current [[Mexican Academy of Sciences]] (1959). He was invited and incorporated into a number of commissions and councils for university institutions. When he died in October of 2007, he was a member of the ''Comisión Especial del Consejo Universitario'' (CECU, Spanish for ''Special University Council Commission'') for the ''Congreso Universitario'' (Spanish for ''University Congress'').<ref name=":0" /><ref name=":1" />
== Honors and commemorations ==
Juan Manuel Lozano Mejía belongs to the generation of academics that UNAM recognizes as "forgers of science" due to his personal and institutional contributions.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Cátedras, medallas y premios, Instituto de Física - UNAM, México |url=https://www.fisica.unam.mx/convocatorias/quien_fue.php |access-date=2023-10-12 |website=Instituto de Física - UNAM, México |language=es}}</ref>

Since 2004, a "Juan Manuel Lozano Mejía" medal and diploma is granted to outstanding physics students associated to UNAM's Physics Institute. <ref name=":0" /><ref name=":1" />
